item.title: Now there’s a sign for how you like to get high
item.description: The Leafly Cannabis Guide employs a set of flower-shaped symbols — set in a kaleidoscope of simple shapes and colours — to lead people through the dizzying array of cannabis strains the legal market has on offer.

item.title: Canada’s first year of cannabis legalization going out on a high
item.description: From product shortages in the early days to edibles on the horizon, we’ve come a long way in our first year of legal weed. Yet one thing remains clear: there’s still much room for improvement when it comes to enforcing…

item.title: They’re immigrants to Canada. So why are they supporting far-right parties that want to reduce immigration?
item.description: This week’s federal election saw some immigrants and people of colour supporting far-right populist parties often accused of xenophobia and racism. Experts say it’s more common than you may think.

item.title: Hamilton homes have toxic lead pipes carrying water to taps
item.description: The city says it will take 40 years to fix the system

item.title: Her landlord didn’t tell her the home she rented had lead pipes — and he didn’t have to
item.description: The reality is the same for renters across the country who live in homes with lead pipes. Many aren’t informed of the risks to themselves and their families. And even if they do know, there’s little they can do but…

item.title: Tainted water: Removing lead pipes is the only way to eliminate risk. But it’s expensive
item.description: The costs often fall to homeowners. In smaller the problem falls to seniors and those who can’t afford several thousand dollars to dig up the pipes.

item.title: ‘I was sleeping with one eye open’ — Canadian cannabis growers harvest their first (legal) outdoor plants
item.description: Finishing up with the first outdoor harvests this week, growers large and small reflect on the experience for the Toronto Star.

item.title: A Canadian vanishes from a Mexican resort town. His daughter unearths disturbing details
item.description: Frustrated by slow police and consular response, Madsen’s daughter has investigated her father’s yearlong disappearance and unearthed disturbing details of events in Puerto Vallarta on Oct. 28, 2018.

item.description: More than a million packages hit GTA doorsteps every single day. Star reporter Brendan Kennedy worked undercover with a courier contracted by the online retail giant to see how it actually gets its packages into people’s hands hours after they’ve…

item.title: ‘Pacifist.’ ‘Activist.’ ‘Scapegoat.’ The rise and fall of Peter Sloly, the Toronto police reformer taking the blame for the ‘Siege of Ottawa’
item.description: Sloly, Ottawa’s first Black police chief, was hired as a reform-minded outsider, a role his supporters say had already made him a marked man. Then came the trucks.
